commits.message: Markdown's <kbd> says it ends with its block, where Rich's stack carries it on; walk drops its dead root (rich-unfiled-791c.k2zi)

Markdown draws <kbd> text in markdown.kbd, its close popping Rich's style stack as Rich 15's does (rich-unfiled-791c.k2zi)

Inline HTML carries its tag as written, and one rule, kbdTags, serves both
inline passes. An image reads its link off the style stack as Rich's
ImageItem does, replacing the separately tracked link.

Segment.divide cuts each segment once at every cut inside it, so wrapping a long line is linear (rich-unfiled-791c.vzmy) (#466)

* Segment.divide cuts each segment once at every cut inside it, so wrapping a long line is linear in its length (rich-unfiled-791c.vzmy)

cutCells takes every position in one walk; Segment.cutAt applies it with each
piece's anchor shifted, and splitCells is its one-cut case. The Markdown
linearity guards now time drawing, not only reading.

* cutCells stops at its last cut, cutAt is private, and Markdown's draw guards are named for and sized to what they time (rich-unfiled-791c.vzmy)

A single cut near the start of a long segment walked and segmented all of it:
splitCells(80) on 1,000,000 ASCII characters took 131 ms, 0.45 ms now. cutAt has
two callers that keep its cuts in range, so it is private rather than a public
method with an unchecked precondition. The million-space link guard reads at
its old size and draws at 50,000: drawing it at a million took 9.4 s.

* cutCells says its positions stop one short of the text's width, where the last piece comes from (rich-unfiled-791c.vzmy)
